status: diagnostic; no production source, public API, threshold, or baseline change
question: Can tsdown grouping make theme and theme/core exports share references while retaining a lean theme/core graph and focused-entry identity?

protocol.builds: Each candidate config built successfully in a package-shaped consumer checkout from the same source revision.
protocol.graphs: Five deterministic graph scans per package entry and format.
protocol.initialization: One excluded fresh-process warmup plus 15 retained fresh-process module-evaluation samples per runtime and format; process startup excluded; forced GC before and after; one sequential cohort per layout; OS cache state uncontrolled.
protocol.identityAndBehavior: Resolve @opsydyn/crumbs-css through its declared export map in one consumer with one React peer; import ESM and require CJS, compare exported references, and render six mixed ThemeProvider/useTheme pairings per runtime.
protocol.redaction: Absolute checkout, temporary directory, and Node executable prefixes in retained JSON are replaced with stable placeholders; sourceSha256 records the original scratch digest for redacted JSON files.

initialization.qualification: Diagnostic only: one cohort per layout. No layout passes all four existing initialization limits.

failures: ESM: keeps the lean theme-core graph independent of optional theme feature chunks
CJS: keeps the lean theme-core graph independent of optional theme feature chunks

decision: Retain the current split. The pair layout adds 94,894/99,135 bytes to the theme/core ESM/CJS graph and loses focused-entry references. Grouping all six theme entries adds 66,495/73,110 bytes to theme/core. Both candidates fail the existing lean-core isolation assertions. Node SSR mixed-provider/hook rendering succeeds with the current split despite distinct exported function references; that result is limited to the tested Node consumer, React peer, and JS realm.
limitations: This does not qualify Expo/Metro, Hermes, a simulator, or a physical device.
Initialization timing is a single diagnostic cohort per layout; do not claim a timing gate pass.
Existing graph zero-growth references remain unchanged and current source is not fully budget-qualified.
Node mixed-entry success does not prove cross-realm or multiple-copy React interoperability.
Android/device acceptance remains parked and last.
